data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 posits that independent operators are 'unlikely to converge on identical design specifications and implementations,' but supplies no causal mechanism enforcing or sustaining that divergence. Its own counterconditions concede plausible mechanisms for homogenization (economic incentives to copy successful designs, best-in-class dependency monoculture), yet the core mechanism treats design diversity as inherent rather than produced. The problem asks what evidence distinguishes truly independent failures from cryptic common-cause failures; SRC_002 offers a post-hoc indicator (divergent failure signatures under identical stress), but provides no causal account of why independent operation would maintain the design diversity required to produce those divergent signatures, leaving the central claim under-mechanized.
